t: Maximum Distance Between Unequal Words in Array I
o: We need the largest j-i+1 over pairs of indices holding different words. In example 1 the differing pair spans the whole array giving 3; in example 2 the best pair is index 1 to 4 giving 4; in example 3 all words are equal so the answer is 0. With n ≤ 100 an O(n^2) scan is trivially fast, but there is also an O(n) observation: the optimal pair can always involve index 0 or index n-1.
k: If words[0] != words[n-1] the answer is simply n.

a.i: Try every pair (i, j) with i < j and track the maximum distance whenever the words differ. With n ≤ 100 this is at most ~5000 comparisons.
s: Loop i from 0 to n-1, loop j from i+1 to n-1.
If words[i] != words[j], update the answer with j - i + 1.
Return the answer (0 if never updated).
a.t: O(n^2) — all pairs checked, trivial for n ≤ 100

a.i: Any maximal-distance unequal pair can be replaced by one touching index 0 or n-1 without shrinking it: if words[0] != words[n-1] the answer is n; otherwise scan for any word different from words[0] at index i and take max(i+1, n-i).
s: If the first and last words differ, return n.
Otherwise, for each i with words[i] != words[0], the best pair uses i with either end: candidate max(i+1, n-i).
Return the maximum candidate, or 0 if all words are equal.
a.t: O(n) — single scan after one comparison

w: In an interview, state the brute force first, then derive the endpoint argument — it shows pattern-recognition skill. Pitfalls: forgetting the all-equal case (return 0) and off-by-one errors since distance is j-i+1, not j-i. Follow-ups: what if distance were j-i, or if you needed the pair itself?
